\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
&&F&&\\

### 1. At least two coins must be moved

The triangle contains four triples of mutually touching coins:

\[
ABD,\qquad BDE,\qquad BCE,\qquad DEF.
\]

If only one coin were moved, at least one of these four triples would remain completely untouched. However, in the desired ring, no three coins are mutually touching—each coin touches only its two neighbors. Therefore, one move cannot suffice, so at least two coins must be moved.

### 2. Two moves are sufficient

Keep \(A,B,E,\) and \(F\) in place. They form four consecutive positions of the desired hexagonal ring. Move:

- \(C\) to the upper-left missing position \(Q\),
- \(D\) to the upper missing position \(P\).

The resulting arrangement is

\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
&&P&&F\\
&Q&&E&\\
&&A&&B
\end{array}
\]

where every adjacent pair is touching, forming the required circle of six coins.

Thus the smallest number of coins that must be moved is

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
